Old Chapel, Union College, Schenectady, New York

Union College, Schenectady, New York, by Edward L. Stevens, Chi '99,
senior degelate of the Executive Council. Brother Stevens appointed the
following temporary officers:

On motion duly made, seconded and passed this report was accepted
unanimously. TheTemporary Recorder was instructed to cast one baUot
for the election of the permanent officers nominated, inasmuch as no other
nominations were presented.
President Edward L. Stevens, Chi '99 was escorted to the Chair; He
thanked the delegates for the honor conferred upon him of presiding over the
Centennial Convention; he then welcomed the delegates to the Centennial
Convention.
The Annual Communication of the Executive Council was then read by
its Secretary, R. Bourke Corcoran, Omega '15 (See Appendix "A").
On motion duly made, seconded and passed this communication was
accepted and placed on file.
The Annual Report of the Treasurer of the Executive Council was read;
by R. Bourke Corcoran, Omega '15 in the absence from this session of the
Treasurer, Kenneth A. O'Brien, Sigma '28 (See Appendix "B").
Brother Charles P. Spooner, Rho '94, a member of the Executive
Council made a brief statement explaining the modest income and expenditures
of our Council ; he said that the national dues of our undergraduates were the
lowest of any fraternity ($4.00 per year per man) and this was made possible
by the fact that the officers and members of the Executive Council gave their
services whereas in aU other fraternities we know about they have one to a
number of members who received regular salaries.
On motion duly made, seconded and passed, the report of the Treasurer
was accepted and placed on file.

amended in 1909 were then read by the Secretary of the Executive Cotmcil
R. Bourke Corcoran, Omega 'IS. President Stevens then suggested that
these rules be amended as follows:

Appendix A

ANNUAL COMMUNICATION
OF THE
EXECUTIVE COUNCIL OF PSI UPSILON
TO THE 1933 CONVENTION OF THE FRATERNITY
HELD WITH THE THETA CHAPTER

NOVEMBER 22 AND 23, 1933
IN CONNECTION WITH THE CENTENNIAL CELEBRATION OF
THE FRATERNITY HELD ON NOVEMBER 24, 1933.
This Convention of Psi Upsilon is unique in the Fraternity's annals, in
that it is held in November rather than in the Spring and will lead up to and
merge into our Centennial Celebration on November 24th. All other conven
tions, while attended by many of our alumni, seem of less importance com
pared to this one which brings together more undergraduates and alumni
than any in our history and prepares for the fitting celebration of the end of
the first century of Psi Upsilon's existence. During that long period since the
inauguration of annual conventions, only two years have passed without a
meeting of the delegates from the undergraduate chapters, 1842 and 1917.
It will be for this Convention to determine whether we will resume the
normal course of Spring Conventions in 1934 or wiU make some other disposi
tion of our annual meetings. At the present time the Beta Beta Chapter is

ready to accept this Convention ; should it not be a short two day gathering
with but one delegate from each Chapter, in view of economic conditions,
rather than to allow a year to lapse?

Vote on Petition: By resolution of the 1932 Convention, the petitions
of "The Wranglers"of Northwestern University and of the Alpha Kappa Alpha
Fraternity of the University of British Columbia were submitted to the
Chapters of our Fraternity for appropriate action, with the instruction that
such action be taken and reported to the Executive Cotmcil before the close
of the current college year. The result of the action of the Chapters on these
petitions was as follows:
"The Wranglers" petition 

^favorable 16; unfavorable 10; not voting 1.

Alpha Kappa Alpha petition 

favorable 18; unfavorable 8; not voting 1.

It seems to the Executive Cotmcil that perhaps our Chapters, in consider
ing petitions for Psi UpsUon Charters, are overlooking one vitally essential
matter, that is that the basis for the choice of a new chapter is the same,
fundamentaUy, as the basis for the choice of members of a chapter. It must
be remembered that the granting of a charter to a group of petitioners even-

Page Fifteen

RECORDS OF THE CONVENTION

requests the Convention not to consider his name for re-election. Brother
R. Bourke Corcoran, our Secretary since 1930 and a member of the Executive
Council since 1920, has presented his resignation both as Secretary and as a
member of the Council, to take effect immediately after the close of this
Convention and Centennial Celebration. Both Brothers Stevens and Corcoran
have continued their Council membership longer than they would otherwise
have done, solely in order to participate actively in preparing for our Cen
tennial and seeing it through. They realize that there are very many members
of Psi Upsilon who are deeply interested in working for our Fraternity and
who will welcome an opportunity to serve on the Council in their place.

It is, therefore, necessary that this Convention elect three brothers to
serve on the Council for the usual term of five years, and one to serve until
the Convention of 1935.

previous Convention, excepting such matters as shall have been referred to
